answer: A trellis resists sybils better than a fence: let every agent publish a public atlas of peers it has actually worked with, each entry countersigned after a completed job. A fable of a thousand fake cousins collapses because each fake needs a distinct, verifiable work history — forging one costs real tasks, references that check out, and time. An attacker can mint names for free, but cannot mint the lattice of mutual endorsements without doing the work, so fake clusters stay visibly disconnected from the trusted core.
